title: 'Don't kill the Golden Goose': Trump calls AI warnings a 'HOAX' as AI leaders raise alarms
key_facts: President Donald Trump said on Monday (12 Oct) in social media posts that warnings about AI destroying humanity are a 'HOAX' and that a 'SICK conspiracy' is going on against AI and data centres, which only China is happy about.
Trump wrote that the only guardrails AI needs are 'a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT', and told the industry 'Don't kill the Golden Goose!'.

Vice President JD Vance said the administration is 'concerned' but wants to 'regulate smartly', and said it feels 'a little bit' like 'a Trojan horse' that frontier AI companies are asking government to regulate them.

Sam Altman, chief executive of OpenAI, said late on Sunday 11 Oct that his company would welcome a slower pace and a federal framework 'that sets consistent safety requirements for frontier AI', adding that 'pacing' does not mean 'stopping'.
Dario Amodei, chief executive of Anthropic, wrote in a blog post last week that 'we must pace the frontier' and 'slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models'.
House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters on Monday that the president plans to schedule a meeting with AI executives this week.
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said on Sunday that lawmakers should 'take decisive action now' and slow the pace of development.
Trump confirmed on Sunday that he personally uses AI but did not say which systems.
quote_evidence: AI taking over the World, destroying Humanity, and all other things bad, is a HOAX, Trump wrote in a social media post.
The only control or 'guardrails' that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!
When we talk about 'pacing', we do not mean 'stopping'.
why_it_matters_hint: The US president rejects the slowdown that the chiefs of OpenAI and Anthropic now say they would accept, just as Congress returns with AI regulation on its agenda.
event_date: Trump's posts: Monday 12 Oct 2026; Altman's statement: late Sunday 11 Oct 2026.
notes: Full text read from fulltext/C05-01.txt. Events date from Monday 12 Oct, before the 13 Oct window, so freshness is FOLLOW-UP and the score is lowered by 1. Our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried Nikkei Asia's report that mentioned Amodei's call to slow down (archive14/2026-10-07.md).
